target_customer: Households in Indonesian tier 2, tier 3 and rural cities buying fresh produce through local agents
problem: Households spend hours at night markets and pay more; Bakool uses a group buying model with community agents to deliver cheaper fresh produce.
business_model: Group buying commerce through an agent network, margin on produce

founders.name: Ivan Darmawan
founders.background_notes: Over 15 years in retail, farming and supply chain per TechNode

founders.name: Stephanie Wongsoredjo
founders.background_notes: Similar background per TechNode; leadership at Southeast Asian unicorns

technical_complexity.rationale: Commerce app and agent tooling; the hard part is supply chain and agent operations.

defensibility.rationale: Agent networks and sourcing density in smaller cities are slow to replicate, though larger commerce players could expand.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence found of incumbents copying the agent model in small cities.

market_need_then: Company claimed savings of up to 15 percent and up to five hours per household, with agents earning up to three times prior income; demand evidence is company statements only.

rebrands.why: Rebranded alongside the seed round; reason not stated in sources

brand_strength.rationale: Rebrand covered by regional tech press, but no evidence of brand driven growth.

pivots.from: Radius, quick commerce for groceries (about 80 percent of orders were fresh goods)
pivots.to: Bakool, group buying of fresh produce via agents
pivots.why: Fresh goods dominated transactions, per DailySocial

outcome_analysis: Bakool pivoted from the Radius grocery model toward fresh produce group buying after seeing most orders were fresh goods, then raised a seed round from US and Asian funds in December 2022. No later round or revenue figure was found, so the traction and outcome are not established.
notes: Seed size undisclosed; one aggregator lists $7.0M and Briter $125K, both unverified. Founding year not confirmed. Name meaning not found. Company website bakool.id not fetched.
